meta.titre: Alcohols and carboxylic acids: ethanol, ethanoic acid and esters

sections.contenu_markdown: Palm wine tapped in the Western Highlands is sweet in the morning, strong by evening, and sour by the next day. The sugary sap is fermented by yeast to ethanol, and then bacteria in the air turn the ethanol to ethanoic acid, the same acid that gives vinegar its sharp taste. Ethanol is also the active ingredient in hand sanitisers and a fuel in some countries. Alcohols and carboxylic acids are two homologous series that come up every year in the GCE O/L organic chemistry questions, usually with ethanol and ethanoic acid as the examples.

items: Carbon atoms form four covalent bonds.
A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen.
Acids turn blue litmus red and react with carbonates to give carbon dioxide.
Fermentation is the breakdown of sugar by yeast, and it makes ethanol and carbon dioxide.

sections.titre: Homologous series: the alcohols and the carboxylic acids
sections.contenu_markdown:
A **homologous series** is a family of organic compounds with the **same general formula**, the **same functional group** and **similar chemical properties**. Each member differs from the next by one $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group, and the physical properties (such as boiling point) change gradually along the series.

**Alcohols** have the functional group **-OH** and the general formula $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$. **Carboxylic acids** have the functional group **-COOH** and the general formula $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}COOH}$.

| Carbon atoms | Alcohol | Carboxylic acid |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Methanol, $\mathrm{CH_{3}OH}$ | Methanoic acid, $\mathrm{HCOOH}$ |
| 2 | Ethanol, $\mathrm{CH_{3}CH_{2}OH}$ | Ethanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_{3}COOH}$ |
| 3 | Propan-1-ol, $\mathrm{CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}OH}$ | Propanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_{3}CH_{2}COOH}$ |
| 4 | Butan-1-ol, $\mathrm{CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}CH_{2}OH}$ | Butanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}COOH}$ |

The names come from the stem (meth = 1 carbon, eth = 2, prop = 3, but = 4). Alcohols end in **-anol** and acids end in **-anoic acid**. The **first member** of the alcohols is methanol and the first member of the carboxylic acids is methanoic acid.

The smaller alcohols and acids are colourless and dissolve in water. Boiling points rise as the chains get longer.

**Key reactions of ethanol:** it burns, $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH + 3O_{2} \rightarrow 2CO_{2} + 3H_{2}O}$ and reacts with sodium to give hydrogen. **Key reactions of ethanoic acid:** it is a **weak acid**, so it turns litmus red, reacts with reactive metals, bases and carbonates to give a salt, and reacts with alcohols to give esters.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how ethanol is made or what it does
variantes.contenu_markdown:
**Manufacture.** (1) **Fermentation** of glucose by yeast at about 30 to 35 $^\circ$C without air: $\mathrm{C_{6}H_{12}O_{6} \rightarrow 2C_{2}H_{5}OH + 2CO_{2}}$ (2) **Hydration of ethene** with steam, using a phosphoric acid catalyst at high temperature and pressure: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{4} + H_{2}O \rightleftharpoons C_{2}H_{5}OH}$

**Reactions.** With sodium it gives off hydrogen: $\mathrm{2C_{2}H_{5}OH + 2Na \rightarrow 2C_{2}H_{5}ONa + H_{2}}$ With phosphorus pentachloride ($\mathrm{PCl_{5}}$), any compound with an -OH group gives off **steamy white fumes of hydrogen chloride**. Acidified potassium dichromate(VI) (orange to green) or bacteria in air oxidise it to ethanoic acid: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH + O_{2} \rightarrow CH_{3}COOH + H_{2}O}$ Heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at about 170 $^\circ$C, it loses water to give ethene: $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH \rightarrow C_{2}H_{4} + H_{2}O}$

variantes.quand_utiliser: When an acid reacts or an ester is made
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Ethanoic acid is a **weak acid**. It reacts with a metal, a base and a carbonate:

$\mathrm{2CH_{3}COOH + Mg \rightarrow (CH_{3}COO)_{2}Mg + H_{2}}$

$\mathrm{CH_{3}COOH + NaOH \rightarrow CH_{3}COONa + H_{2}O}$

$\mathrm{2CH_{3}COOH + Na_{2}CO_{3} \rightarrow 2CH_{3}COONa + H_{2}O + CO_{2}}$

**Esterification.** An alcohol and a carboxylic acid are warmed with a few drops of **concentrated sulphuric acid**, which acts as a catalyst, to make an **ester** and water:

$\mathrm{CH_{3}COOH + CH_{3}CH_{2}OH \rightleftharpoons CH_{3}COOCH_{2}CH_{3} + H_{2}O}$

The ester is **ethyl ethanoate**. Esters have sweet, fruity smells and are used in perfumes and food flavouring.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When two colourless liquids must be distinguished
variantes.contenu_markdown:
| Test | Ethanol | Ethanoic acid |
|---|---|---|
| Universal indicator | Green (neutral) | Orange or red (acidic) |
| Add sodium carbonate | No reaction | Fizzing; carbon dioxide turns limewater milky |
| Add magnesium ribbon | No reaction | Fizzing; hydrogen |

sections.enonce_markdown: A brewer ferments a solution that contains 90 g of glucose with yeast. ($A_r$: C = 12; H = 1; O = 16; 1 mole of gas = 24 dm$^3$.) (a) Write the balanced equation. (b) Calculate the maximum mass of ethanol that can be formed. (c) Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide given off at room temperature and pressure. (d) The actual yield is 80%. Calculate the mass of ethanol obtained.

etapes.justification: Yeast converts glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide.

etapes.action: Find the moles and mass of ethanol.
etapes.justification: 1 mol of glucose gives 2 mol of ethanol. $M_r(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}) = 24 + 6 + 16 = 46$.

etapes.action: Find the volume of carbon dioxide.
etapes.justification: 1 mol of glucose also gives 2 mol of carbon dioxide.
The actual mass is the yield percentage of the maximum mass.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The maximum mass of ethanol is **46 g**, with **24 dm$^3$** of carbon dioxide, and an 80% yield gives **36.8 g**.

items.erreur_markdown: The members of a homologous series all have the same physical properties.
items.pourquoi_faux: Their chemical properties are similar, but their physical properties, such as boiling point, change gradually as the chain gets longer.
items.correction_markdown: Same functional group means similar chemistry; boiling points **rise** along the series.

items.erreur_markdown: Ethanoic acid is a strong acid like hydrochloric acid.
items.pourquoi_faux: Ethanoic acid ionises only slightly in water.

items.erreur_markdown: Ethanol is acidic because it contains an -OH group.
items.pourquoi_faux: The -OH of an alcohol does not ionise to give hydrogen ions in water. Ethanol is neutral.
items.correction_markdown: A solution of ethanol has pH about 7 and does not change the colour of litmus.

items.erreur_markdown: An alcohol and a carboxylic acid react to form a salt and water.
items.pourquoi_faux: That is the result of an acid and a base. An alcohol is not a base. The product is an ester.
items.correction_markdown: Alcohol + carboxylic acid $\rightleftharpoons$ ester + water, with concentrated sulphuric acid as a catalyst.

items.erreur_markdown: The first member of the carboxylic acids is ethanoic acid.
items.pourquoi_faux: Ethanoic acid has two carbon atoms. The first member has one carbon atom.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Write the general formula of the alcohols and name their functional group. (b) Write the formula of propan-1-ol and of propanoic acid. (c) Which two of $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH}$, $\mathrm{CH_{3}COOH}$ and $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{7}OH}$ belong to the same homologous series?
items.solution_markdown: (a) $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$; the functional group is **-OH** (hydroxyl). (b) $\mathrm{CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}OH}$ and $\mathrm{CH_{3}CH_{2}COOH}$. (c) **$\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH}$ and $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{7}OH}$**: both are alcohols and differ by one $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group.

items.enonce_markdown: A sample of 6.0 g of propan-1-ol, $\mathrm{C_{3}H_{7}OH}$, is burnt completely in oxygen. ($A_r$: C = 12; H = 1; O = 16; 1 mole of gas = 24 dm$^3$.) (a) Write the balanced equation. (b) Calculate the volume of oxygen needed. (c) Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide and the mass of water formed.

Ethanoic acid reacts with propan-1-ol to make an ester. ($A_r$: C = 12; H = 1; O = 16.) (a) Write the equation, name the ester and state the catalyst and conditions. (b) Calculate the maximum mass of ester from 6.0 g of ethanoic acid with excess alcohol. (c) The yield is 70%. Calculate the actual mass of ester. (d) Describe a chemical test that distinguishes ethanoic acid from propan-1-ol.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $\mathrm{CH_{3}COOH + CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}OH \rightleftharpoons CH_{3}COOCH_{2}CH_{2}CH_{3} + H_{2}O}$ The ester is **propyl ethanoate**; the catalyst is a few drops of **concentrated sulphuric acid** and the mixture is warmed. (b) $M_r(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}) = 60$, so $n = 0.10$ mol. The ester $\mathrm{C_5H_{10}O_2}$ has $M_r = 60 + 10 + 32 = 102$, so the maximum mass is $0.10 \times 102 = $ **10.2 g**. (c) $10.2 \times 0.70 = $ **7.14 g**. (d) Add sodium carbonate solution: ethanoic acid gives **fizzing** and carbon dioxide that turns limewater milky; propan-1-ol gives no reaction.

items_markdown: A homologous series has the same general formula and functional group, similar chemistry and a gradual change in physical properties.
Alcohols: $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$ (-OH). Carboxylic acids: $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}COOH}$ (-COOH). First members: methanol and methanoic acid.
Ethanol is made by fermentation of glucose or by hydration of ethene, and it burns, reacts with sodium and is oxidised to ethanoic acid.
Ethanoic acid is a **weak acid**: it reacts with metals, bases and carbonates.
Alcohol + carboxylic acid gives an **ester** and water, using warm concentrated sulphuric acid as catalyst.
